standard.title: Present and distribute with planning
standard.description: present media arts works to audiences and plan approaches for creating relationships with audiences if/when media arts works are distributed in selected personal, community and/or institutional contexts using responsible media practice
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can present media arts works in informal and formal settings applying responsible media practices. They can reflect on how different audiences receive the same work. They have not yet planned distribution strategies, investigated classification systems, or engaged with government regulation, self-regulation and institutional media producer relationships.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students present media arts works to audiences and plan approaches for creating audience relationships in personal, community and/or institutional distribution contexts using responsible media practice.

nodes.label: Distribution planning and audience relationships
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a distribution approach for a media arts work — identifying the target audience, platform, and strategies for creating audience relationships in that distribution context.
nodes.minimum_width: Plan a distribution approach for a media arts work — identifying one platform, the target audience, and at least two strategies for creating audience relationships in that context.
nodes.typical_width: Plan distribution approaches across personal, community and institutional contexts; research how different audiences relate to media arts works and how those relationships inform production and distribution; investigate how intended audiences and the communities they form influence the creation of new works.
wider: Investigate the relationships created between intended audiences and media arts works — including the communities formed between audience members — and use this research to plan a distribution strategy that deliberately cultivates specific audience relationships

Plan distribution for a media arts work across two different contexts (e.g. school LMS and community event) — comparing how each context creates different audience relationships and evaluating which best serves the work's purpose
nodes.hinge_reason: Distribution planning is prerequisite to actual distribution — without a plan that addresses audience relationships, responsible media practice is applied reactively rather than strategically, and the 'plan approaches' command term is not met.

response_modes.reason: Use structured planning: 'Who is the intended audience? How does this platform create or limit the relationships I want? What responsible practice requirements apply in this context?' Distribution decisions are relationship decisions.

success_criteria: Student can identify a target audience, platform, and at least two audience relationship strategies for a planned distribution
Student can explain how the platform choice serves the intended audience relationship

nodes.label: Regulatory and ethical frameworks
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate classification systems and regulatory frameworks and apply relevant requirements to production and distribution decisions.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one classification or regulatory requirement relevant to a planned distribution (e.g. Australia's classification system for one media platform) and explain how it affects production or distribution decisions.
nodes.typical_width: Research Australia's classification system across platforms; investigate differences between government regulation and self-regulation; apply classification thinking to production decisions; produce guidelines for ethical online conduct; apply ICIP rights and copyright requirements to distribution.
wider: Investigate Australia's classification system across different media platforms — analysing the impact of classification requirements on producers and audiences, and applying classification analysis to decisions made in their own production and distribution process

Research differences between government regulation and self-regulation in media production and distribution — comparing how different media producers (sole digital, multi-platform, cross-media, public and private sector) develop audience relationships, and applying findings to plan distribution of original work

response_modes.reason: Regulatory and ethical frameworks are integrated into distribution decision-making — support students in treating classification, ICIP rights and copyright as distribution design considerations, not external compliance requirements added at the end.

Vary the regulatory and ethical frameworks investigated — classification, ICIP, copyright, government vs self-regulation, platform-specific safety — to build genuine range across the full spectrum of responsible distribution practice.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of regulatory and ethical contexts at Y9-10 (classification systems, ICIP rights, copyright, government vs self-regulation, platform-specific online safety) is genuinely diverse — students who investigate across multiple frameworks develop much more sophisticated production citizenship.
success_criteria: Student can identify at least one classification or regulatory requirement relevant to their distribution context
Student can explain how that requirement shapes specific production or distribution decisions
